claire_docs: Quick FYI — ran into a surprising behavior in the Python SDK while trying to parse nested structured output from a tool call in an async streaming context. Looks like nested lists (line_items) are being dropped when a client-side timeout cancels the stream, even though server completed successfully.

maria_devex: Oof. Can you paste a tiny repro?

claire_docs: Yep. Minimal example below (using pydantic dataclasses for structured output):
```python
import asyncio
from redwood import RedwoodClient
from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import List

class LineItem(BaseModel):
    sku: str
    qty: int

class Invoice(BaseModel):
    invoice_number: str
    line_items: List[LineItem]

client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${RW_KEY}")

async def main():
    # server tool streams tokens then emits final structured JSON matching Invoice
    resp = await client.call_tool_stream("invoice_tool", payload="...", timeout=0.8)
    # resp.structured should be Invoice model
    print(type(resp.structured), repr(resp.structured))

asyncio.run(main())
```

Observed (0.12.3): prints "<class 'dict'> {'invoice_number': 'INV-555', 'line_items': []}" — line_items empty, server logs show full list present.

sam_backend: Which SDK version? repro on CI?

claire_docs: 0.12.3 locally and in CI. Downgrading to 0.12.0 returns the expected nested list.

dinesh: I captured a trace. When timeout triggers we cancel the stream task which short-circuits the parser; the SDK tries to coerce partial tokens into structured output and falls back to empty defaults for missing arrays. The server actually sent the full JSON; client cancelled right before finalization, but our stream handler was still able to fetch final frame if we didn't cancel racing futures.

sam_backend: So it's a cancellation vs drain race. We introduced an aggressive timeout wrapper in 0.12.2 that cancels underlying reader immediately. Older behavior allowed a short drain window.

claire_docs: Right. The user impact is pretty bad for onboarding sample apps that rely on structured models (example sample-app invoice parser). New users see empty lists and think tool is broken.

sam_backend: I'll open RW-issue-8012. Short-term fix: relax timeout logic to attempt to drain remaining frames for 200ms after cancellation before falling back. Long-term: make structured parsing atomic — buffer final json body before parsing, even for streamed responses, unless user opts-in to incremental parsing.

ci-cd-bot: New issue created: RW-issue-8012 - "py-sdk: streamed toolcall cancellation drops nested structured fields"

maria_devex: Can you include a unit/integration test that simulates a delayed final frame to reproduce reliably? Also update the sample-app to pin SDK version or include a note.

sam_backend: Adding test that uses a mocked stream with delayed final chunk. Also adding an env var toggle RW_STRICT_STREAMING to let advanced users keep old behavior. Will prepare a small PR.

claire_docs: Pulled the branch, test passes locally and sample-app now shows full line_items. I also updated the docs repo with a short troubleshooting note and a snippet showing how to increase timeout or set RW_STRICT_STREAMING for low-memory environments.

sam_backend: PR #4538 opened. Patch includes: 1) 200ms drain window on timeout, 2) atomic buffer-before-parse for structured outputs, 3) unit + integration tests, 4) changelog entry. Will request review from eng-ml because parser touches inference code paths.

maria_devex: Thanks — recommend backport to 0.12.4 and a developer note for the sample-app quickstart so new users don't hit this.

ci-cd-bot: PR created: 4538. CI: queued.

sam_backend: CI green and review from eng-ml approved. Merging and creating backport branch.

claire_docs: Verified merged package fixes the sample-app on a fresh container. Leaving a short blurb in the README and adding a tiny e2e check in the sample-app workflow to assert nested arrays are present.

maria_devex: Great work. Filing a quick follow-up to consider exposing structured parse failure metrics in the Console so we can detect regressions when users upgrade SDKs.

sam_backend: Good idea. Filing RW-issue-8013 for metrics.

ci-cd-bot: RW-issue-8013 created: "metrics: structured parse fail rates for toolcalls (py sdk)"

claire_docs: Thanks folks. Leaving the minimal repro as a gist in the docs repo and adding a short note in the FAQ about timeouts + streaming structured outputs. :thumbsup:
